Cc: procurement@nexahealth.com, itsec@nexahealth.com

Subject: Edge-hosted private install — access & audit exception request

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the demo last week. Nexa's legal and IT security reviewed Redwood's private/VPC offering and we have two non-standard asks before we can proceed to PO:

1) Audit window: Our compliance team needs the ability to pull a full-forensic snapshot for an annual audit. We request a 72-hour on-prem inspection window where our auditors can run checks against logs and a subset of host-level artifacts.

2) Troubleshooting access during onboarding: We need a way for our security operations engineer to run a troubleshooting session if we hit infra issues in the first 90 days. They request temporary host-level access under strong controls (session recording, time-limited credentials).

Both items are blockers for our procurement committee. Separately, because of the onboarding effort and the extended support exposure, procurement is asking if Redwood can provide a one-time concession on list pricing (they're targeting ~5%) in exchange for a 12-month commit and an earlier go-live.

I've attached the HITRUST/supply chain questionnaire and a proposed SLA spreadsheet (redacted). Can you route this to the right people for exec sign-off if necessary?

Attachments: Nexa_HITRUST_questionnaire.pdf, proposed_multiparty_sla.xlsx

Thanks,
--
Alice Tan
Director, Procurement
Nexa Health

Subject: Re: Edge-hosted private install — access & audit exception request

Alice — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Looping in Rishi (deals), Laura (legal), and Markus (ops exec) to review the two asks.

Quick proposed approach from my side to make this tractable:
- Audit snapshots: Redwood policy is no routine host-level snapshots shared to customers. For annual audits we can provide an export path (immutable logs, indexed events, and a pre-defined forensic bundle). We can agree to a controlled inspection workflow. We prefer a 48-hour supervised window vs 72 hours — operationally safer for our hosts.
- Troubleshooting access: we can support time-limited, audited jump-host sessions (ephemeral keys, session recording, SSO enforced) for the first 90 days of onboarding. Access would be strictly scoped and require a signed access request + co-signed NDA addendum.

On pricing — happy to escalate. Nexa's ask for ~5% off list for 12 months is reasonable to discuss; would prefer to trade lower discount (3%) for a 12–18 month commit and a short SLA uplift during onboarding.

Asking Rishi and Markus for exec sign-off on bending the audit window to 48 hours and approving a 3% concession, and Laura for legal to confirm language for the DPA amendment and access request flow.

Cc'd Nexa IT Sec so they can comment on the exact data set needed for the audit snapshot.

Thanks,
--
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Looping my thoughts in — thanks Camila.

Operational constraints + commercial recommendation:
- Audit window: Operationally we prefer to keep host-level access out of regular customer flows. From experience, a 48-hour supervised window with a clearly defined artifact list (logs, container images metadata, KVM snapshots if absolutely necessary) is the safest compromise. Approve only if Nexa signs the DPA addendum and provides a local SOC/lead for supervision.
- Troubleshooting access: we can do ephemeral jump-host sessions (SSO enforced, session recording stored to a KMS-encrypted bucket) for the first 90 days. Access revoked immediately after the session. That resolves most of the risk.

Commercial: given the onboarding and monitoring burden, I recommend a 3% one-time concession (not recurring), contingent on a 12-month minimum commitment and a mutually agreed SOW for the onboarding scope. If Nexa insists on 72 hours or continuous host access, we should decline or ask for a higher concession.

Laura — can legal prepare a short DPA addendum template and an access request template we can present to Nexa? Markus — can you confirm operational feasibility of the session recording + KMS storage? If you approve, Camila can present the package (3% discount, 48-hour supervised audit window, ephemeral session controls) to Nexa.

Thanks,

Approved with conditions — thanks for the clear options. Executive decision below: 

1) Commercial: approve a one-time 3% concession off list pricing for deal DW-9032, conditioned on a signed 12-month minimum and receipt of PO by 2026-12-15.

2) Audit window: approve a supervised 48-hour forensic inspection window (not 72). The inspection must be:
   - Scheduled at least 30 days in advance,
   - Performed under Redwood supervision with Nexa's auditor given read-only access through a jump-host,
   - Session recording and artifact export stored in a KMS-encrypted S3 bucket; access logs retained for 7 years per our retention policy.

3) Troubleshooting access: approve ephemeral host access for onboarding only (first 90 days). Implement controls: time-limited ephemeral keys, SSO & MFA required, full session recording, and a signed access request template. No permanent host credentials or unmanaged SSH access.

4) Legal & Security: Laura to prepare the DPA addendum and access request template; Security to sign off on the exact artifact list allowed during inspection.

5) Final sign-off doc: Camila, please attach exec_approval_DW-9032.pdf to the offer and send the DocuSign envelope to Nexa (use the linked envelope). We will not start any host-level work until PO + signed DocuSign returned.
